summary: Engineered a high-performance system foundation focusing on two pillars: memory retrieval and API throughput. Implemented a two-stage Quantized Vector Memory (QSV) engine using BQ and SQ8 for efficient long-term retrieval, and an AsyncWorkerPool with semaphore-based concurrency control to optimize Gemini API interactions.
key_learnings: Binary Quantization and SQ8 reduce vector footprints by up to 96% with minimal loss in recall, outperforming raw FP32 storage.
Asyncio-based queue management with semaphore control is critical for maximizing API throughput while maintaining compliance with rate limits.
Prototyping infrastructure natively (e.g., NumPy) before relying on external dependencies ensures a lean, optimized codebase.

summary: This cycle focused on optimizing CI/CD overhead by refactoring GitHub Actions matrix builds to reduce runner bloat and improve feedback loops. I researched strategic pruning and caching techniques, and proposed a dynamic pruning utility to calculate a 'Minimum Viable Test Matrix' based on dependency requirements.
key_learnings: Moving from brute-force matrix expansion to explicit 'include' blocks significantly reduces resource waste.
Cache keys must be scoped to matrix dimensions to prevent cache pollution across different environments.
Dynamic matrix generation adds efficiency but requires a fail-safe fallback to prevent CI pipeline blockage.
